title: Multi-ring / hole-aware patch boundary walker
description:
`PatchBoundaryWalker.extract` currently bails (returns null) when a patch's boundary isn't a single simply-connected ring — e.g. patches with internal holes (concavity carve-outs sit inside them) or patches whose boundary pinches into two separated rings. On voyage_skull_ref.obj with PATCH-16's settings, ~34 of 71 patches hit this path, including the big cranium patch. These patches skip Coons evaluation entirely and fall back to shape-proxy-only behavior.

Fix: when the neighbour map has a vertex with 3+ boundary neighbours or disconnected subgraphs, identify the **outermost boundary ring** (largest by vertex count or enclosed area) and use that for the 4-corner extraction. Inner holes get ignored for Coons purposes — those interior voids are already separate concavity patches, so the outer ring is what the Coons fit is actually trying to approximate.

Alternative if that's too fragile: split hole-ful patches preemptively at the concavity boundary so every final patch is simply-connected.

Critical files:
- ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/data/PatchBoundaryWalker.java — `extract` method, line ~55.
- Test case: voyage_skull_ref.obj's cranium patch (currently ~13k vertices, sides=247 per boundarySideCount, fourSided=false in my walker).

Acceptance: Coons-fit-succeeded count in /tmp/DebugCoons.java rises from 34 to near 67 (all non-trivial patches get a Coons error).
definition-of-done:
1. `PatchBoundaryWalker.extract` handles multi-ring boundaries by walking the outer ring.
2. Non-manifold junctions (3+ boundary neighbours at a vertex) are resolved by picking the two neighbours that continue the outer ring.
3. Skull: 90%+ of patches successfully get a Coons error computed (up from ~48% today).
4. No regression in the already-working 4-corner walker path.
testing-plan:
1. Run /tmp/DebugCoons.java on skull — expect nullWalks to drop from 33 to near 0.
2. Run VerifyCoonsError — expect nonzero-error vertex count to rise from 4504 to closer to 20k (most of the mesh now getting measured).
3. Regression: small/simple patches with clean rings still produce the same 4 corners they do today.
